facts.statement: Sazavis was an enantiornithine bird that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Sazavis was an enantiornithine bird from the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Sazavis likely lived in the region now known as the Kyzyl Kum desert in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: It might have been related to Nanantius and lived in what is now the Kyzyl Kum of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: Only one species of Sazavis is currently known to science, named Sazavis prisca.
facts.quote: There is a single species known to date, Sazavis prisca.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Sazavis is a single tibiotarsus bone that is approximately 4.5 millimeters wide at its distal joint.
facts.quote: It is only known from a single piece of tibiotarsus about 4.5 mm wide in a distal joint.

facts.statement: Sazavis was roughly the size of a pigeon, measuring about 18.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The bird was the size of a pigeon, approximately 18.5 cm long in life.

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Sazavis were discovered in the Bissekty Formation.
facts.quote: The bone has been found in the Bissekty Formation.

facts.statement: Sazavis lived during the Turonian stage, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sazavis belongs to the parent group Alexornithidae.
Sazavis likely inhabited coastal areas or liman forests dominated by flowering plants from the Platanaceae family.
facts.quote: Sazavis possibly lived on nearby coasts or in the liman forests dominated by the flowering plants of the Platanaceae family.
